title: Molecular speeds at two temperatures
caption: Nitrogen molecules have a spread of speeds. At 300 K the most probable speed is about 422 m s⁻¹; at 600 K the curve flattens and shifts right to about 597 m s⁻¹. The area under each curve, the total number of molecules, is the same.
alt: Two Maxwell–Boltzmann speed distributions for nitrogen: a taller, narrower curve peaking near 420 m/s at 300 K and a lower, broader curve peaking near 600 m/s at 600 K.
description: 300 K: a peak at about 422 m s⁻¹.
600 K: lower, broader, peaking at about 597 m s⁻¹.
Both start at zero, and both curves enclose the same area.

checks.name: 300 K: most probable speed √(2RT/M) = 422 m s⁻¹
